Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Start time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Elliot Park (CEO); Maya Patel (VP Eng); Jordan Kim (Head of Product); Sam Rivera (Head of Sales); Priya Nair (Head of People); ~120 attendees via webinar + remote offices (EU/APAC)

Company all-hands covering Q2 results, a brief incident review for an EU region outage last week, product roadmap highlights, go-to-market progress, hiring/people updates, and Q&A. Leadership shared next steps, follow-up docs to be shared, and action items assigned.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Elliot: Alright, good morning everybody, welcome to the July all-hands. Uh, I know a lot of you are remote and, ah, some of our folks in EU joining late evening so thanks for being here. I'll kick off with a quick scoreboard, Maya's gonna walk the incident, Jordan will do product, Sam on sales, Priya on people and then we'll open for Q and A.

[00:28] Elliot: Quick numbers — Q2 we ended up about 12% above our internal plan on ARR growth, bookings were up mostly because of Dedicated contracts, which is great. That said, renewals slipped a bit, uh, especially with one mid-market account where things got delayed by procurement. So mixed, but overall momentum.

[01:05] Maya: Thanks Elliot. I wanna talk about the EU region outage from last Thursday. Quick, I mean, root cause was a networking change pushed by our infra provider that triggered a mismatch with our autoscaler policy — the autoscaler underestimated cold-starts on some GPU pools, and combined with a routing fallback mis-config, we saw elevated latencies then partial errors.

[01:35] Maya: We rolled a mitigation in 45 minutes, full recovery in about two hours, but we had residual increased latency for the rest of the day on a small subset. We're doing a full postmortem, documenting timeline, and will publish mitigation steps and long-term fixes — including tighter canary windows, additional fallback model variants, and improved observability on the KV cache warm-up states.

[02:10] Attendee (Speaker 12): sorry quick question — will this affect our SLAs with Dedicated customers?

[02:18] Maya: Short answer: no immediate SLA breaches, we hit degraded performance windows that are within some terms but we are notifying customers proactively. For dedicated customers we have isolation guarantees; the incident primarily impacted hosted region capacity. We're following up with affected customers; ops will offer credits where appropriate — Jordan will coordinate comms with CSMs and Sam on AE outreach.

[02:45] Jordan: On product — big focus areas for Q3: 1) Dedicated autoscaler improvements and burst capacity guarantees, 2) Private deployment beta (VPC + on-prem installer) going into two pilot customers, 3) Redwood Optimize features — smarter batching suggestions and quantization profiles for common workloads. We'll have early access docs soon and a workshop for SEs so you can run customer benchmarks.

[03:20] Jordan: We're also prioritizing faster kernel selection heuristics and ops tools to reduce cold-starts; these are directly tied to the incident mitigations Maya mentioned. We wanna make serving predictable across modes — hosted, dedicated, private — same API, same expectations.

[03:50] Sam: Sales update — pipeline is better quarter-over-quarter; largest expansion deals are in late-stage with three enterprise prospects asking for Dedicated + Private evaluation. Main blocker is procurement and security review cycles, which is where we need faster turnaround on SSO/SAML docs, SOC2 evidence, and KMS integrations. I've asked security to prioritize a standard pack we can share.

[04:20] Sam: Also, pricing feedback — customers are asking for clearer unit economics when you compare quantized Dedicated runs vs hosted; Jordan and Maya are working on standard benchmark artifacts we can cite in RFP responses.

[04:45] Priya: People update — hiring: we've reopened reqs for infra engineers and SEs, adding two L4 infra hires and three SEs targeted in Q3. Culture: we'll run a cross-functional offsite late August, and we'll open the employee feedback survey after this meeting. Also quick reminder — parental leave policy updates are live in the handbook.

[05:15] Attendee (Speaker 48): question on Private beta — do customers need to be on-prem or can they use a VPC setup?

[05:22] Jordan: Both. The beta supports VPC deployments with customer-managed networking; the on-prem package is optional for fully air-gapped customers. We'll share the beta eligibility doc after the call.

[05:40] Elliot: Ok folks, a few quick remarks on strategy: our thesis hasn't changed — serving is the differentiator. We are investing where it matters: predictability (SLOs), cost controls (batching/quantization), and deploy flexibility. The market — OpenAI/Anthropic — continue to iterate fast; our differentiation is the developer-first, production-grade experience with cost transparency.

[06:10] Elliot: Please remember for enterprise engagements, show the benchmarks and explain the tradeoffs — latency vs cost, dedicated isolation vs hosted speed of onboarding. That's a key conversation for AEs.

[06:30] Q&A snippet (varied speakers):
[06:35] Speaker 73: Are we expanding to more cloud regions?
[06:38] Maya: Yes, EU expansion continues and APAC region work is in progress; timeline depends on capacity and partners (we're evaluating an N. Asia edge partner).

[06:50] Speaker 85: Will we open-source any of the runtime improvements?

[06:52] Jordan: Short answer: some components — not all. We'll keep some optimizations internal for product differentiation, but expect tooling and evaluation harnesses to be public.

[07:05] Speaker 90: Any change to pricing?

[07:08] Sam: No planned broad changes. We may introduce clearer unit pricing for quantized profiles and a Dedicated burst tier pricing option next quarter. We'll share a pricing note.

[07:30] Cross-talk: (brief interruptions, multiple speakers)
[07:38] Elliot: We're hitting time so quick closing notes — thanks to ops for mitigation work last week, thanks to sales for new pipeline, and to everyone for the product work.

[07:50] Elliot: We'll publish the Q2 deck and the incident postmortem; expect an email with links. Also, leaders please keep calendars open for the roadmap workshop the week after next.

[08:05] Priya: Please fill out the engagement survey — it's anonymous, and we use it to plan the offsite and improve remote work support.

[08:22] Final rapid-fire topics:
- Legal update (short): license templates being refreshed to reduce procurement friction — legal will push a standard clause pack to AE/SE.
- Security: SOC2 renewal in progress; we have a scheduled audit in Q3.
- Ops: working on better KV cache warm-up instrumentation.

[09:00] Recap and next steps:
- Leadership to share Q2 metrics deck and incident postmortem (Elliot/Maya)
- Product to share beta eligibility + early access docs (Jordan)
- Sales to get packaged security/SOC2 docs for AEs (Sam + Security)
- People Ops to run survey and summarize (Priya)

[09:35] Elliot: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.
